intro: Japanese points with a set of words that share endings and change only the first sound. こ- is near me, the speaker. そ- is near you, the listener, or something one of us has just mentioned. あ- is away from both of us, or something we both remember. ど- asks which. The ending tells you the job: -れ is a thing on its own, -の comes before a noun, -こ is a place, -んな means 'this kind of', and こう / そう / ああ mean 'in this way'. So every choice is two questions: whose territory is it, and what job does the word do in the sentence?

skills.rule: これ / それ / あれ stand alone as 'this one / that one': これ near me, それ near you, あれ away from both of us.
skills.explain:
これ, それ and あれ are pronouns: they replace a noun and take particles directly, これは, それを, あれが. Use これ for a thing near me or in my hand, それ for a thing near you or in your hand, あれ for a thing away from both of us. The question word is どれ 'which one' (out of three or more).

Territory belongs to people, so it flips when the speaker changes. If you hold something up and ask これは何ですか, I answer それは... because, from my side, it is near you. When we stand side by side looking the same way, the territory is shared: これ is near us both, それ a little way off, あれ far away.

They are for things, not people. Pointing at a person with これ or あれ sounds rude; say この人 or, politely, こちら. They also never stand before a noun: 'this book' is この本, not これ本.
patterns: これ / それ / あれ は [noun] です
これ / それ / あれ を [verb]
どれ が [noun] ですか

examples.jp: {これ}は何[なん]ですか。
examples.en: What is this?

examples.jp: {それ}は私[わたし]の傘[かさ]です。
examples.en: That one (by you) is my umbrella.

examples.jp: {あれ}は富士山[ふじさん]ですよ。
examples.en: That over there is Mount Fuji.

examples.jp: すみません、{それ}を見[み]せてください。
examples.en: Excuse me, could you show me that one (by you)?

examples.jp: {どれ}が田中[たなか]さんのかばんですか。
examples.en: Which one is Mr Tanaka's bag?

contrast.vs: この / その / あの
contrast.note: これ stands alone; この must have a noun after it. これは本です 'this is a book', この本は高い 'this book is expensive'.

contrast.vs: ここ / そこ / あそこ
contrast.note: これ points at a thing, ここ at a place. ここは駅です 'this (place) is the station', これは切符です 'this is a ticket'.

mistakes.bad: {これ}本[ほん]はおもしろいです。
mistakes.good: {この}本[ほん]はおもしろいです。
mistakes.note: Before a noun use この, not これ.

mistakes.bad: 「これは何[なん]ですか。」「{これ}は辞書[じしょ]です。」
mistakes.good: 「これは何[なん]ですか。」「{それ}は辞書[じしょ]です。」
mistakes.note: The thing is near the person who asked, so the person answering says それ.

skills.tip: In my hand: これ. In yours: それ. In neither: あれ. If a noun follows, switch -れ to -の.

skills.rule: この / その / あの must be followed by a noun: 'this book', 'that bag', 'that building over there'.
skills.explain:
この, その and あの work like 'this' and 'that' in front of a noun, and they cannot stand alone. The territory rule is the same as for これ / それ / あれ: この本 is the book near me, その本 the book near you, あの本 the book away from both of us. The question word is どの 'which (noun)': どの電車に乗りますか.

This is the set to use for people: この人, あの人 'that person over there', and politely この方, あの方. あの人 is also how you refer to a person both of you know who is not present.

The common error is mixing up the two endings. -れ ends the phrase: これは. -の needs a noun: この本は. If you would say 'this one' in English, use これ; if you would say 'this + noun', use この. Note that この already contains の, so これの本 is wrong too.
patterns: この / その / あの + [noun]

examples.jp: {この}本[ほん]はおもしろいです。
examples.en: This book is interesting.

examples.jp: {あの}人[ひと]は誰[だれ]ですか。
examples.en: Who is that person over there?

examples.jp: {その}かばん、どこで買[か]ったんですか。
examples.en: Where did you buy that bag (you're carrying)?

examples.jp: {この}電車[でんしゃ]は東京[とうきょう]に行[い]きますか。
examples.en: Does this train go to Tokyo?

examples.jp: {あの}白[しろ]い建物[たてもの]は病院[びょういん]です。
examples.en: That white building over there is a hospital.

contrast.vs: これ / それ / あれ
contrast.note: No noun after it: これ. A noun after it: この. これは高い 'this one is expensive', この時計は高い 'this watch is expensive'.

contrast.vs: こんな / そんな / あんな
contrast.note: この本 is this particular book; こんな本 is a book of this kind.

mistakes.bad: {この}は私[わたし]のペンです。
mistakes.good: {これ}は私[わたし]のペンです。
mistakes.note: この cannot stand alone; with no noun after it, use これ.

mistakes.bad: {これの}かさは誰[だれ]のですか。
mistakes.good: {この}かさは誰[だれ]のですか。
mistakes.note: この already includes の; これの + noun is wrong.

skills.tip: Is the next word a noun? Then -の: この, その, あの, どの. Otherwise -れ.

skills.rule: ここ / そこ / あそこ name a place (here, there by you, over there); こちら / そちら / あちら are the polite forms, also used for directions and people.
skills.explain:
ここ is the place where I am, そこ the place where you are or near you, あそこ a place away from both of us; どこ asks where. Note the irregular form: あそこ, never あこ. They are nouns, so they take particles: ここに置いてください, あそこで待ちます.

こちら / そちら / あちら / どちら are the polite versions. They point at a place or direction (こちらへどうぞ 'this way, please'), and they are the polite way to point at a person: こちらは山田さんです 'this is Mr Yamada'. In shops and on the phone they are the default; on the phone, そちら means your end: そちらは今何時ですか 'what time is it there?'. どちら also means 'which of two'. The casual forms are こっち / そっち / あっち / どっち.

Use これ for things and ここ for places: pointing at a building, あれは病院です 'that is a hospital'; telling someone where it is, 病院はあそこです.
patterns: ここ / そこ / あそこ は [place] です
[thing] は ここ / そこ / あそこ に あります
こちら は [person] です
こちら へ どうぞ

examples.jp: トイレは{あそこ}です。
examples.en: The toilet is over there.

examples.jp: {ここ}に名前[なまえ]を書[か]いてください。
examples.en: Please write your name here.

examples.jp: {そこ}に座[すわ]ってもいいですよ。
examples.en: You can sit there (by you).

examples.jp: {こちら}へどうぞ。
examples.en: This way, please.

examples.jp: {こちら}は営業部[えいぎょうぶ]の山田[やまだ]さんです。
examples.en: This is Mr Yamada from the sales department.

contrast.vs: これ / それ / あれ
contrast.note: これ is a thing, ここ a place. Introducing a person: こちらは..., never これは...

contrast.vs: この / その / あの
contrast.note: Before a noun use この: この部屋 'this room'. ここ before a noun needs の and means 'of this place': ここの料理 'the food here'.

mistakes.bad: {この}に荷物[にもつ]を置[お]いてください。
mistakes.good: {ここ}に荷物[にもつ]を置[お]いてください。
mistakes.note: この needs a noun after it; the place word is ここ.

mistakes.bad: {これ}は私[わたし]の上司[じょうし]の鈴木[すずき]さんです。
mistakes.good: {こちら}は私[わたし]の上司[じょうし]の鈴木[すずき]さんです。
mistakes.note: Introducing a person with これ treats them as an object; use こちら.

skills.tip: Can you answer 'where?' with it? Then it is ここ / そこ / あそこ. Talking to a customer or about a person? Make it こちら.

skills.rule: こんな / そんな / あんな + noun mean 'this kind of'; こう / そう / ああ + verb mean 'in this way, like that'.
skills.explain:
こんな / そんな / あんな / どんな describe the kind of thing, and they come directly before a noun: こんな本 'a book like this', そんなこと 'that sort of thing', どんな映画 'what kind of film'. Compare この本, which is this particular book.

こう / そう / ああ / どう describe the way something is done, and they come before a verb: こう書いてください 'write it like this', どう読みますか 'how do you read it?'. そう is also the everyday word for agreeing or reporting: そうです, 私もそう思います, そうですか.

For degree ('this much', 'so'), add に to the -んな form and put it before an adjective or verb: こんなに高いとは思わなかった 'I didn't think it would be this expensive', そんなに食べないで 'don't eat so much'. The territory rule still holds: こんな for what I show or describe, そんな for what you just said or did, あんな for something away from both of us or remembered together. そんな and あんな often carry surprise or disapproval: そんなこと言わないで.
patterns: こんな / そんな / あんな / どんな + [noun]
こう / そう / ああ / どう + [verb]
こんなに / そんなに + [adjective]

examples.jp: 私[わたし]も{そう}思[おも]います。
examples.en: I think so too.

examples.jp: {こんな}かばんがほしいです。
examples.en: I want a bag like this.

examples.jp: 名前[なまえ]は{こう}書[か]いてください。
examples.en: Please write your name like this.

examples.jp: {そんな}ことは言[い]っていません。
examples.en: I didn't say anything like that.

examples.jp: いつか{あんな}大[おお]きい家[いえ]に住[す]みたいです。
examples.en: Someday I'd like to live in a big house like that one.

contrast.vs: この / その / あの
contrast.note: この映画 is this particular film; こんな映画 is a film of this kind. Ask yourself whether you mean 'this' or 'like this'.
Same meaning, different partner: こんな before a noun (こんな字), こう before a verb (こう書く).

mistakes.note: A verb follows, so use the manner word こう, not こんな.

mistakes.bad: 私[わたし]も{そんな}思[おも]います。
mistakes.good: 私[わたし]も{そう}思[おも]います。
mistakes.note: 思う is a verb; 'think so' is そう思う.

skills.tip: Noun next: こんな / そんな / あんな. Verb next: こう / そう / ああ. If English says 'so' or 'like that' with a verb, it is そう.

skills.rule: For something mentioned rather than seen, use あれ / あの when both of us know it from experience, and それ / その when only one of us does.
skills.explain:
When the thing is not in front of you, territory becomes knowledge. あ- points at something that both speaker and listener know first-hand: a place you went together, a person you both know, a matter you discussed before. あの店、また行きたいね means the shop we both remember.

そ- points back at something that has just come up in the conversation but that only one of you knows: what the listener has just told you, or what you are telling them about that they have not seen. If a friend says 'I met someone called Suzuki', you ask その人は誰？, not あの人, because you do not know Suzuki. If you tell someone about a café they have never been to, it is そのカフェ.

In writing, refer back with そ- (or この for the topic under discussion: この問題は...); あ- appears only for the writer's own memories. これ / この refer to what I am saying or about to say: これは秘密だけど 'this is a secret, but...'.
patterns: [just mentioned, only one of us knows it] → それ / その + [noun]
[what I am about to say] → これ

examples.jp: 去年[きょねん]一緒[いっしょ]に行[い]った{あの}店[みせ]、また行[い]きたいね。
examples.en: I'd like to go back to that shop we went to together last year.

examples.jp: 「鈴木[すずき]さんって知[し]ってる？」「ううん、{その}人[ひと]、誰[だれ]？」
examples.en: 'Do you know Suzuki?' 'No, who's that?'

examples.jp: 「財布[さいふ]をなくしたんです。」「{それ}は大変[たいへん]でしたね。」
examples.en: 'I lost my wallet.' 'That must have been awful.'

examples.jp: 先週[せんしゅう]話[はな]した{あの}件[けん]、どうなりましたか。
examples.en: What happened with that matter we talked about last week?

examples.jp: 昨日[きのう]、駅前[えきまえ]のカフェに行[い]きました。{その}カフェはケーキがおいしかったです。
examples.en: Yesterday I went to a café near the station. That café had delicious cakes.

contrast.note: Telling someone about an inn they have never seen (京都で古い旅館に泊まったよ。): その旅館. Reminding a friend of an inn you stayed at together: あの旅館、よかったね.
これ points at what I am saying now or about to say: これは内緒だよ 'this is between us'. It does not point back at what the listener said.

mistakes.bad: 「新[あたら]しい先生[せんせい]に会[あ]ったよ。」「{あの}先生[せんせい]はどんな人[ひと]？」
mistakes.good: 「新[あたら]しい先生[せんせい]に会[あ]ったよ。」「{その}先生[せんせい]はどんな人[ひと]？」
mistakes.note: The listener has not met the teacher, so it is その, not あの.

mistakes.bad: この前[まえ]一緒[いっしょ]に見[み]た{その}映画[えいが]、おもしろかったね。
mistakes.good: この前[まえ]一緒[いっしょ]に見[み]た{あの}映画[えいが]、おもしろかったね。
mistakes.note: Nothing was just mentioned, and you both saw the film: a shared memory is あの. その would point back at something just said.

skills.tip: Ask: have we both seen it? Yes: あ-. Only one of us: そ-.
